title: Render-mode flag bits ([e+0x61C68]) and WIL slot-grid literals (slots 62-139): bit semantics, writer provenance, mode-map, and full literal pinning
objective: Close pending items [2] (render-mode flag bit semantics) and [4] (slot grid 82-86 / 90-127 literal names) of docs/research/ei-ui-layout/player-composition-evidence.json; refine pending item [3] (weapon/head selector 41..50 / 21..29 landings) with static proof.
question: 1) Which code paths set the bits of the render-mode dword [e+0x61C68]? Are any bits computed client-side, or do they all originate from descriptor/server data? What behavioral meaning does each reader attach to its bit? Are the 'mode words' produced by the 0x404DA0 resolver pure alpha/color-key blit constants with no other effect? 2) What literal WIL path strings occupy slot-grid slots 82-86 and 90-127 (and surrounding 62-139), and how do they map to element indexes?
method: Exhaustive raw-byte scan of Mir3.exe .text for the disp32 0x61C68 (25 hits = 24 unique instructions: 17 writers + 8 readers + 1 misaligned false hit at 0x404B55's disp); targeted disasm of every hit; setter-family classification; reader-side semantic reconstruction with surrounding-frame analysis; resolver map extraction at 0x404DA0-0x404E0C; dispatcher walk at 0x404E10; rep-movsd block-pairing simulation over the unrolled slot-grid init 0x4534B0-0x454120 (capstone detail + skipdata; state machine on lea edx,[ebx+disp] / mov edi,edx / mov edi,imm / rep movs*); GBK/ASCII literal decode; wilsdk spot checks; cross-ref with Findings 280/282 and the element table 0x5600FC.
source: Mir3.exe (/tmp/nas_mnt/NAS/TMP/EI传奇3.0客户端/Mir3.exe); image base 0x400000; fileoff = VA - 0x400000; code/data 0x400000-0x47FFFF
verdict: Both pending items closed with primary-static proof: (1) [e+0x61C68] bits are exclusively server/descriptor-driven (17 wholesale-copy writers, no client-side bit computation; exhaustive scan), with reader-defined semantics bit 0x1 = race 0x53-0x55 special frame-lock gate, bit 0x2 = name-tag visibility, bit 0x100000 = spawn/teleport white flash, bit 0x8000000 = half-speed, and the six mode bits acting only as blit-mode/alpha/color-key constants via the 0x404DA0 map + 0x404E10 dispatcher; (2) slot grid 62-139 literals fully pinned (82-86 = Inventory/Equip/Ground/MIcon/ProgUse, 90-107 = Mon-3..Mon-20, 108-127 = MonS-1..MonS-20, plus NPC/MonMagic/MonImg/hair/helmet/DMon/MagicEx/StoreItem), element index == slot index. Pending item [3] (weapon/head selector) refined: landings proven static (0x40C7B7-0x40C85D); only the runtime/server trigger for sel>40 remains open.

conclusions.claim: [e+0x61C68] bits are NEVER computed client-side: exhaustive raw-byte scan of .text for the disp32 (25 hits = 24 unique instructions + 1 misaligned false hit) yields exactly 17 writer sites and 8 reader sites. Every writer copies a descriptor dword wholesale (from [esp+X] caller frame) or assembles it from two descriptor words (0x40D6E4: flags=(word[edx+8]<<16)|word[edx+6]); the ctor zeroes it (0x404B55). Every setter that has a 'test al,2' path also mirrors bit 0x2 into [e+0x61BD0]. Bits therefore originate from descriptor/server data at runtime; no flag arithmetic exists client-side.
conclusions.va: 0x40D6E4 (representative writer); all 17 writers listed in 'writers' section

conclusions.claim: Bit 0x1 = special frame-lock gate for race 0x53-0x55 (83-85): at 0x407197/0x40AF55 `test byte [esi+0x61C68],1; je skip`; when set, type byte [e+0x88]==3 reads a 16-bit race from [e+0x8A]/[e+0x8B] else byte [e+0x8A]; race in [0x53,0x55] → call [vtable+0x10], lock flag byte [e+0xC0]=bl, and single-frame span [e+0xB8]=[e+0xB4]+1; 0x40AFAB clamps the +0x61C7C span 2→3. Crossref: Finding 280 (monster codes 83-85 have no monster.json records).

Bit 0x2 = name-tag visibility: every setter mirrors it with `test al,2; je; mov [esi+0x61BD0],1` (e.g. 0x4069E0, 0x40D6E4); the mirror is also written by the per-entity visibility loop 0x419EDE/0x419EF2 (call 0x424360; [e+0x61BD0] = 0 or 1); readers 0x40B75A and 0x40C908 test [e+0x61BD0] and skip the floating name-label blit when 0. Confirms bit 0x2 == 'show name tag'.

Bit 0x100000 = spawn/teleport white-flash gate: 0x40CE2B `test [esi+0x61C68],0x100000; je done; GetTickCount(0x47630C) - [e+0x62A2C] > 0x6A4 (1700ms)` → flash blits from the 0x8AB7BC icon buffer; the timer field +0x62A2C is armed at 0x411239 when state byte [e+0x62A38]==0x1F and the bit is clear (then set at runtime by the state transition).

Bit 0x8000000 = half-speed animation: 0x405D21 (in the frame-reset family, preceded by `mov byte [esi+0x61C7D],5`) `test [esi+0x61C68],0x8000000; je; mov edx,[esi+0xBC]; shl edx,1; mov [esi+0xBC],edx` doubles the frame interval; independently 0x40AFFF/0x40D12D increment [e+0x61C84] (reset at mod 0x186A0) and `test byte [e+0x61C84],1; jne skip` — odd ticks skip the frame advance, drawing every other frame.

The six mode bits have NO behavioral effect beyond blit-mode selection: resolver 0x404DA0-0x404E0C maps 0x800000→1, 0x4000000→0, 0x20000000→0xFBFF, 0x10000000→0xFFE0, 0x8000000→0x94BF, 0x40000000→0xFCB2, 0x80000000→0x7E0, default 0xFFFF (returned in eax; side-store `mov word [ecx+0x61C6C],0xFFFF` at 0x404E03; ret 0x404E0C). Dispatcher 0x404E10 consumes the word: mode 0x1 → 0x404E41 → DDraw blit 0x461ED0 (800x492 args 0x320/0x1EC); modes 0x94BF/0x0/0x7E0 → 0x404F63; default → 0x404E9E (via [e+0x61C58] selects 0x463330 or 0x460240; dsurface 0x8AB7A8; ret 0x28). Mode words are pure alpha/color-key blit constants. Note 0x8000000 is BOTH mode 0x94BF and the half-speed bit.

Slot grid literals fully pinned for slots 62-139: dest = 0xB130 + slot*0x104 (140 slots total); the unrolled init block 0x4534B0-0x454120 copies each literal (rep movsd pairing: dest = previous block's `lea edx,[ebx+disp]`, source = previous tail's `mov edi,<litVA>` after strlen) — 78 copies decoded. Slots 82-86 = Inventory/Equip/Ground/MIcon/ProgUse (element 0x52-0x56); 90-107 = Mon-3..Mon-20; 108-127 = MonS-1..MonS-20; 128 = NPC; 129 MonMagic; 130 MonImg; 131-134 = M-Hair/M-Helmet1/WM-Hair/WM-Helmet1; 135/136 = DMon-1/DMonS-1; 137 MagicEx; 138 MonMagicEx; 139 StoreItem; 70 GameInter (+0xF848); 71 M-Hum; 76 WM-Hum (+0xFE60); 81 Magic (+0x10374); 62-69 = Snow tail (dungeonsc/innersc/furnituresc/wallsc/smobjectsc/animationsc/object1c/object2c). Element index == slot index (ten element==slot checks incl. 0x47=71, 0x4C=76, 0x51=81, 0x57=87, 0x58=88, 0x80=128, 0x83=131, 0x84=132, 0x85=133, 0x87=135).

Element==slot mapping derived (cross-check): element byte E selects slot E of the grid; verified for E in {0x47,0x4C,0x51,0x57,0x58,0x80,0x83,0x84,0x85,0x86,0x87,0x8B} against the init dest arithmetic; consistent with the source file's six original cross-checks and with Finding 280's '槽 N' numbering (280 base 0xF848 → 280-槽 N == this grid slot N+70; Mon-1 = 280-槽18 = slot 88, NPC = 280-槽58 = slot 128, DMon-1 = 280-槽65 = slot 135).

Weapon/head selector semantics (pending item [3]) now statically proven: 0x40C7B7-0x40C85D computes element = (sel-1)/10 + bias per branch: male (type [e+0x88]==0) head bias -0x7D, weapon bias +0x48; female (type==1) head bias -0x7B, weapon bias +0x4D (magic-const division by 10, result byte [e+0x629CE]). Landings: male weapon sel 1-10→72 M-Weapon1 .. sel 41-50→0x4C=76 WM-Hum; female weapon sel 41-50→0x51=81 Magic.wil; male head sel 1-9→0x83=131 M-Hair, 11-19→0x84=132 M-Helmet1, 21-29→0x85=133 WM-Hair; female head sel 1-9→0x85=133 WM-Hair, 11-19→0x86=134 WM-Helmet1, 21-29→0x87=135 DMon-1. The landings ARE the client-side meaning (extended weapon/head sets stored in those WILs); only the runtime/server trigger (which server appearance codes map to sel>40 / head>20) remains open.

slot_grid.note: slots 62-139 decoded here (78 copies); slots 0-61 are the environment/tile set in the earlier init region (out of scope). element index == slot index. Finding 280 '槽 N' numbering uses base 0xF848, so 280-槽 N == slot N+70 here.

closed_notes: Closed player-composition-evidence.json pending [2] (render-mode flag bit semantics) and [4] (slot grid 82-86/90-127 literals); refined [3] (weapon/head selector landings now statically proven, remaining trigger runtime-only). Corrections recorded: (a) GameInter.wil occupies slot 70 at +0xF848 (matches the source file's base-0xF848 note), NOT the +0xF744 pairing in docs/research/ei-ui-layout/mir3-dat-resource-path-table.json (row 'destination_lea_va 0x004527a4'); 0x4527A4 disassembles to `mov byte ptr [esi+ebp], dl` (string-encode code, not a lea) — the +0xF744 slot belongs to Snow\object2c.wil@0x47CE24. That path-table JSON was left untouched (out of scope). (b) bit 0x1 earlier characterized as a death/type-specific frame-truncation gate is refined to a race 0x53-0x55 (83-85) special frame-lock gate (crossref Finding 280: no monster.json records for codes 83-85). (c) RESEARCH_LOG.md round-6 entry intentionally NOT written by this agent (constraint: do not touch RESEARCH_LOG.md); main agent should append the entry at commit time.
